summary: Red team of the extraction of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, Integral p-adic Hodge theory (Publ. Math. IHÉS 128 (2018) 219–397). All 190 items were re-read against arXiv v3 and the open-access published text; all three recorded hashes match. The item-level reading is good: every numbered statement has an item, most statements are faithful, and E1–E18 are all real. There are 15 findings, 8 medium and 7 low; they concern the routing, two statements the paper itself gets wrong, and missed mistakes. (1) The §4.2 A_inf-module algebra is routed to AI.2, although the accepted RS-01 gives it to AI.5. As routed, AI.2 would need coherence of W_n(O^♭), which is routed to AI.3 and is not upstream of AI.2; the CohomologyComparisons packet plans the same lemmas a third time. (2) Theorem 14.3 (AI.5) uses Proposition 13.21, which is planned at CP.2, downstream of AI.5: a cycle. (3) Theorem 5.7 (AI.4) rests on Scholze's primitive comparison, whose only owner (from PAPER-SCHOLZE-13, which this session wrote) is P8, downstream of AI.4; CP.3's Theorem 13.1 uses Theorem 5.7 without AI.4 upstream. (4) Lemma 9.8, Theorem 10.4 and Corollary 10.2 go to CR.4 but are used in AI.3's proofs. (5) The §2 examples sit at AI.5, but their proofs need CR.3 (Lemma 2.12, Illusie's Enriques computation). (6) Faltings' almost purity, in the local forms the construction uses, and almost-mathematics vocabulary have no items. (7) The converse of Lemma 3.20 is false as printed, and item 047 copies it: it needs p topologically nilpotent. (8) Lemma 11.11's λ_r([T_i]) = U_i should be U_i^{p^r}, and item 162 copies it. Low: three false steps in proofs of true lemmas (6.9, 4.8 — which also makes E2's reason wrong — and 14.5); about 15 unrecorded misprints; inexact item statements and notes; missing items for cited theorems (Berthelot, Illusie, Kisin, Beauville–Laszlo, Kiehl); Lemma 6.1 belongs to E1; Mathlib's BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham are not cited and fontaineTheta's hypotheses are misreported; about a dozen off-by-one-page locators. The review's accept-with-no-changes introduced no new error, but it missed the RS-01 owner conflict (finding 1) and the unlisted Mathlib period rings (finding 14).

sourceVersions.citation: TeX source integralpadicHodge.tex of arXiv v3, the text read line by line
Publ. Math. IHÉS 128 (2018), 219–397, doi:10.1007/s10240-019-00102-z (open access); all quoted pages are its page numbers

checked: Independence. PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 was written by Claude Code cc-442dc5 (issue #1462, PR #2002; provenance line of the .md). REV-PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 was written by Claude Code cc-fb70e5 (PR #2398; review.json notes and reviews/REV-PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18.md). The string cc-f805bf occurs in none of the four target files, and git log shows no commit by this session on them.

Disclosure. This session wrote PAPER-SCHOLZE-13 (p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties) and reviewed PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15 (PR #4673), PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18 (PR #4683) and PAPER-SCHOLZE-17 (PR #4688). Finding 3 touches PAPER-SCHOLZE-13's route 1 (PadicHodgeTheory P8/P8:local-rational): the primitive comparison theorem is routed there, and the finding asks for that route's target to be narrowed to P8:local-rational. Finding 14(a) relies on PAPER-SCHOLZE-13's library citation of BDeRhamPlus/BDeRham, which was re-read at the pin. No finding touches the routes or conclusions of the Kedlaya–Liu, Fargues–Fontaine or Scholze 2017 reviews; Fargues' BKF classification (item 081, AI.2) and Kedlaya's Lemma 4.6 are consistent with the Scholze–Weinstein extraction (AI.2).

Sources. arXiv:1602.03148 has three versions (v1 9 Feb 2016, v2 7 Sep 2018, v3 15 Jan 2019, 'final version'); v3 is the latest, and it is the version the extraction recorded. Both v3 artifacts were re-downloaded on 30 September 2026 and match the recorded hashes: the PDF (sha256 285f7d2088607688365ca92222dcf44c0acd6c4788dd872fe6a6191b9c4e072a) and the e-print (sha256 ff989b40b0864ed79933382c3cc018c0fa1c119bbe50188ece1ea6fc262b5aa4; integralpadicHodge.tex and .bbl). The published PDF from Centre Mersenne (179 pp., sha256 a924d36c8ef92888d9739011f8cc6675f846544c88edb9f670c7ecf2052702bb) also matches. Every finding quoting the paper was checked in both texts; all quoted slips are present in the published version.

Reading. The whole TeX source was read, split among five parallel readers: §§1–3, §§4–5, §§6–9, §§10–12 and §§13–14 with the introduction's main theorems. Each reader compared every item in its range for statement, hypotheses and locator. I personally re-checked every finding filed here at the TeX line and the published page. This includes the counterexamples to Lemma 3.20's converse, to the inclusion in the proof of Lemma 6.9, to the trichotomy in the proof of Lemma 4.8 and to the length identity in the proof of Theorem 14.5, and the invariance computation behind Lemma 11.11.

Coverage. Every numbered statement of §§1–14 has an item, as the review said; the gaps found are unnumbered steps and cited external theorems (findings 6 and 12). I also checked the job brief's named topics: A_inf, θ, ξ, BKF modules, Lη, the pro-étale site, almost purity, AΩ, the comparison theorems, the q-de Rham complex, Koszul complexes, the Hodge–Tate comparison and spectral sequence, the torsion inequality and its mod-p form, Fargues' classification, and the §2 counterexamples (Enriques-type 3-fold and the Z/p^2 degeneration). There is no Kedlaya–Liu vector-bundle material in BMS1 beyond Kedlaya's Lemma 4.6.

Statements. All 190 items were compared with the paper; defects are in findings 7, 8 and 11. Among others, the following hypotheses were checked: proper vs smooth, O_K vs O_C, the torsion-freeness in degrees i and i+1, Remark 14.2's weakening, the replete-topos assumption of §6.2, characteristic 0 vs arbitrary perfectoid fields in §4.2, and finitely presented vs finitely generated.

sourceIssues. E1–E18 were re-checked at their locators in both texts, and all are real. E2's reason is wrong (finding 9). E17 should absorb Proposition 13.15's '(1)' and E18's locator should be pp. 390–391 (finding 10). The 18 recorded issues are misprints only; findings 7–10 add two errors in stated results and three false proof steps, plus about 15 misprints.

Library claims read at the pins (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474). Mathlib: PreTilt (RingTheory/Perfection.lean:634), PreTilt.untilt (RingTheory/Perfectoid/Untilt.lean:49), WittVector (RingTheory/WittVector/Defs.lean:52), WittVector.fontaineTheta (FontaineTheta.lean:165, under the section variables at :118), fontaineTheta_teichmuller (:182), surjective_fontaineTheta (:195), BDeRhamPlus (BDeRham.lean:77), BDeRham (:90), fontaineThetaInvertP (:64), Module.FinitePresentation.trans (Algebra/Module/FinitePresentation.lean:322) and FinitePresentation.of_isBaseChange (:353). The declaration index was searched in both libraries for Koszul, coherent ring, décalage/Lη, K-flat, Artin–Rees (Tau Ceti has only TauCeti.ArtinRees.exists_controlled_lift, for the noetherian lemma), crystalline, Kisin, Breuil, A_inf/Acrys, de Rham–Witt, perfectoid, and Witt-vector étaleness. None of these exists beyond what finding 14 lists, so the 'missing' statuses otherwise hold.

Atlas layers. I read the full stage texts of AInfCohomology AI.0–AI.7, CohomologyComparisons CP.0–CP.6, CrystallineCohomology CR.0–CR.7, PadicHodgeTheory R06.1, P8 and P8:local-rational, PerfectoidSpaces P1–P3, and EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1–E2. I also used the stage texts of PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra, AdicEtaleGeometry A1, DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1 and PrismaticCohomology PR.0/PR.6, as quoted in the items. Each of the 27 cited layers exists and plans its items in the paper's generality, except where findings 1–6 and 13 say otherwise.

Packets and restructurings. I read: RS-01 (owners, layer actions and links for AI.x and CP.x; accepted 23 September); RS-05 (owners of almost algebra, almost purity and the cotangent complex); and the packets AInfCohomology--AI.0 (AI.1 nodes and requests), CohomologyComparisons (all 20 nodes, coverage and requests), PerfectoidQuotients, CrystallineCohomology--CR.0 (CR.4 nodes), FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory (stage counts), PrismaticCohomology--PR.0, AdicEtaleGeometry, DerivedDeRhamCohomology and HabiroCohomologyFoundations--HQ.1 (Koszul-twist node). For every route I checked the dependency order, using data/atlas.json stage edges together with the links of accepted RS results, research/blueprint/links and packets. RS-01's CP.3 → CP.2 link resolves an apparent gap for items 001, 006 and 008, so none is reported.

Other extractions. Searched all accepted paper extractions for the same material: BKF modules and Fargues' theorem (Scholze–Weinstein 20, Guo–Reinecke 24: AI.2, consistent), Kedlaya's punctured-spectrum lemma (Scholze–Weinstein 20: AI.2, consistent), the primitive comparison (Scholze 13: P8, finding 3), Lη and AΩ (BMS 19, Bhatt–Scholze 22: consistent), the cotangent complex of perfect(oid) rings (Scholze 12: P1/DD.0) and Scholze's finiteness theorem (Scholze 13 and this extraction both route it to P8, consistent). Koszul complexes are planned at AI.1, and also used as a model at DD.1, built at IHG.6 and twisted at HQ.1; this was judged an area-level question, so no finding is filed on it.
Checks run: python3 scripts/check_redteam.py on the result (no errors) and python3 research/blueprint/intake.py check-files on both deliverables (0 problems).

findings.claim: The route order has a cycle. Theorem 14.3's assertion that every H^i_{A_inf}(𝔛) is a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module is proved using Proposition 13.21, and the extraction places Theorem 14.3 at AI.5 and Proposition 13.21 at CP.2. CP.2 requires AI.5, so AI.5 would need a statement owned downstream of itself. Item 009's own note records the dependence ('finite freeness after inverting p is Corollary 4.20 with the A_crys and étale comparisons and Proposition 13.21'). Proposition 13.21 is a purely crystalline statement: crystalline cohomology of Y = 𝔛 ×_{Spf O} Spec O/p over A_crys, after inverting p, equals the base change of H^i_crys(Ȳ/W(k)) along a section k → O/p. Its proof uses only that Frobenius is an isogeny and crystalline base change. The CohomologyComparisons packet already asks CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 for exactly those inputs.
findings.evidence: BMS1, proof of Theorem 14.3 (published p. 392): 'It follows that all cohomology groups are finite free after inverting p by Corollary 4.20 and comparisons (iii) and (iv), using also Proposition 13.21. Thus, all cohomology groups are Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules.' Proposition 13.21 (p. 387): 'Fix a section k → O/p. Then there is a canonical φ-equivariant isomorphism H^i_crys(Y/A_crys)[1/p] ≅ H^i_crys(Ȳ/W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} A_crys[1/p]'. Its proof: 'for any qcqs smooth O/p-scheme Z, the Frobenius … is an isomorphism after inverting p … Base change for crystalline cohomology implies the result.' data/atlas.json: CohomologyComparisons:CP.2 requires AInfCohomology:AI.5. The CR.3 stage text owns 'derived base-change maps for crystalline families' and the 'CR.3:Frobenius-isogeny' substage, with 'Sources: … BMS1 §14'. CohomologyComparisons packet request to CR.3: 'Crystalline base change and the Frobenius isogeny … which the source's Proposition 13.21 imports'.
findings.fix: Plan item 189 at CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 (its Frobenius-isogeny and base-change parts) instead of CP.2, and add a stage link CR.3 → AInfCohomology:AI.5. CR.3 requires only CR.2, so this creates no cycle. CP.2 then imports it through its existing CR.3 requirement. Alternatively, give Proposition 13.21 to AI.5 itself. Either way, add the dependency to item 009's note and route text.

findings.claim: Faltings' almost purity theorem is the paper's central external input. Its local group-cohomological forms are what Lη upgrades, and they have no items. Four comparisons are used: RΓ_cont(Γ, R_∞) → RΓ_cont(Δ, R̄^) is an almost quasi-isomorphism; RΓ_cont(Δ, R̄^) = RΓ(X_profet, Ô^+_X) (Scholze 2013, Propositions 3.5 and 3.7(iii), Corollary 6.6); the analogous maps for W_r(R_∞) and for A_inf(R_∞) are almost quasi-isomorphisms with respect to W_r(𝔪) and [𝔪^♭]; and the variant in condition (i) of Lemma 9.12 used in Proposition 9.14 and Lemma 12.8. The almost-mathematics vocabulary these need also has no item: almost zero element, almost quasi-isomorphism, and the W_r(𝔪)- and W(𝔪^♭)-variants, whose idempotence fails, as the paper warns. Item 121 mentions the Ô^+ case only inside a definition. AI.3's stage text asks to 'prove the almost purity comparison', and PerfectoidSpaces P3 (almost purity) and P0 (almost algebra, per RS-05) own the general theory, so the items are planned rather than missing, but the extraction does not record them. The job brief and PROTOCOL §0 both name almost purity among the notions a coverage must outline.

findings.claim: The converse of BMS1 Lemma 3.20 is false as printed, and item 047 copies it: 'Conversely, if R^+ is perfectoid and bounded in R, then R is perfectoid in Fontaine's sense.' The hypothesis that p is topologically nilpotent in R is missing. Counterexample: let A be the (p,T)-adic completion of O_C[T^{1/p^∞}], R = A[1/T] with the T-adic topology on A, and R^+ = A. Then R is a complete Tate ring, and A is an open, bounded, integrally closed subring of R. It is integrally closed because the Gauss valuations v_r(Σ c_e T^e) = min_e(v_p(c_e) + re), r > 0, are multiplicative: if g/T^k is integral over A then v_r(g) ≥ rk for all r > 0, which forces c_e = 0 for e < k. A is perfectoid in the BMS sense: it is p-adically complete, p^{1/p} is a non-zero-divisor with (p^{1/p})^p | p, and Frobenius A/p^{1/p} → A/p is an isomorphism (Lemma 3.10(ii)). But R is not perfectoid in Fontaine's sense. If π were a topologically nilpotent unit with π^p | p in R°, its image under the continuous map A → O_C, T^e ↦ 0 (e > 0), would be nilpotent, hence 0, forcing p ↦ 0 in O_C. The proof fails at its last sentence ('π = θ([π^{♭1/p^n}]) for n sufficiently large has the desired property'): with π_0 = T one gets π ≈ T^{1/p^n}, and π^p never divides p. The forward direction, and the case of a Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (for example any Tate Q_p-algebra), are unaffected. The paper uses only the forward direction later (§5.1).
findings.evidence: BMS1 Lemma 3.20 (published p. 255) and its proof (pp. 255–256), quoted above. Fontaine's definition as recalled on p. 255: 'there is a topologically nilpotent unit π ∈ R such that π^p divides p in R°'. arXiv v1–v3 and the published version were searched, and Crossref lists no erratum or update.

findings.claim: Three steps in proofs are false as written, although the lemmas they prove are true. None is recorded. (a) Proof of Lemma 6.9 (second transformation): 'the sheaf 𝓘^{⊗n} ⊗ C^{n−1} contains (and is thus equal to) the sheaf (η_𝓘C)^{n−1} … the quotient … is easily identified with 𝓘^{⊗n−1} ⊗ H^n(C)[𝓘]'. Counterexample: 𝓘 = (p) over Z and C = Z in degree n−1, zero elsewhere. Then (η_pC)^{n−1} = p^{n−1}Z ⊄ p^nZ, while H^n(C)[p] = 0. The correct statement works modulo cocycles, with 𝓘^{⊗n}C^{n−1} + 𝓘^{⊗(n−1)}Z^{n−1}, which suffices for the map to τ^{≥n}. (b) Proof of Lemma 4.8, case d = 1: 'D is one of three possible modules: a principal fractional ideal, a fractional ideal of the form 𝔪^♭·J …, or K^♭ itself'. The list misses {x : |x| ≤ r} for r outside the value group (for K = C take r = p^{−√2}). The lemma survives, since any non-finitely-generated D has D ⊗ k = 0. Recorded E2 corrects only the wording ('fraction field' → 'fractional ideal'), and its reason repeats the false claim that the three cases classify rank-one submodules. (c) Proof of Theorem 14.5(ii): 'length Tor_1^{W(k)}(Q, W(k)/p^n) = length(Q/p^n), which holds for any torsion W(k)-module'. This is false for Q = W(k)[1/p]/W(k), where Q/p^n = 0 but Tor_1 = Q[p^n] has length n. It needs 'finitely generated', which holds where it is used. Item 007's note states it correctly.

findings.claim: BMS1 has misprints that the extraction and the review did not record. Proposition 4.3 proof, p. 264: 'Z' = {x ∈ 𝔪 | x^p ∈ Z}' omits the Frobenius on W(k)-coefficients, and should be x^p ∈ σ̃(Z); the two agree when k = F_p, and the argument goes through since σ̃ preserves |·|. Lemma 4.6 proof, p. 268: 'so M → M_2/p is injective' should be M/p, and 'dim_k(M/p ⊗_{R_2} k)' (twice) should be ⊗_{O^♭}, since k is not an R_2 = A_inf[1/x]-algebra. Lemma 9.13 proof, p. 329 (twice): 'the proof of Proposition 9.6' should be Lemma 9.6. §12.2, p. 361: 'a natural map S_Σ → A_inf(R_∞,Σ)' cannot exist, since S_Σ is an A_crys-algebra; it should be A_inf[x_u^{±1}] → A_inf(R_∞,Σ) (item 171 already states the corrected map). Lemma 12.8(iv) proof, p. 366: three occurrences of ξ_r should be ξ̃_r, because μ ∈ (ξ_r) and so Lη_μ(C/ξ_r) is undefined. Lemma 13.8 proof, p. 374: 'f(x) ∈ N and … ∈ pN' should read N' = p^nN and pN'; as printed, g' ≡ f' mod p does not follow. Remark 13.17, p. 383: 'purely inseparable over that of k' should be K.
